Answer: B
Reason: Figure 1a (CT) shows a hyperdense foreign body (fishbone) in the esophagus with adjacent extraluminal air, indicating esophageal perforation. Although Figure 2 (CXR) appears relatively clear, pneumothorax or pneumomediastinum is the direct complication of such a perforation, and among the choices, it is the only one mechanistically linked to the visible breach; pleural effusions are not evident on the provided CXR.
